name: Borde / Geroch: topology change is kinematically possible with non-singular Lorentz metrics (Borde's 2-dimensional examples)

source.located: A. Borde, 'Topology Change in Classical General Relativity', arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, 30 Jun 1994. Read: abstract p.1; Sec. I.A (classical evolution, foliation remark); Sec. II.A (interpolating spacetime; 'It is assumed that the metrics being considered are time-oriented'); Sec. II.B (vector field <-> time-orientable Lorentz metric, g = (h(V,V))h - 2 hV hV); Sec. Geroch 1967 (J. Math. Phys. 8, 782), Misner (via ref. [5]), Reinhart 1963 and Sorkin (ref. [13]) are NAMED-NOT-READ: known here only as Borde restates them.

published_statement: Abstract: 'No assumption is made about the dimension of spacetime. First, it is stressed that topology change is kinematically possible; i.e., if a field equation is not imposed, it is possible to construct topology-changing spacetimes with non-singular Lorentz metrics. Simple 2-dimensional examples of this are shown.' Sec. III.C summary: 'if n is odd, there is a spacetime that interpolates between them if and only if chi(S1) = chi(S2) [13] ... If n = 2, then again examples of topology change can be constructed ... if n is even and is greater than 2, then there is always an interpolating spacetime ... Thus, kinematically, though there are some constraints, a large variety of topology-changing closed universes exist. In particular, as Misner has pointed out (see [5]), since any two closed 3-manifolds are cobordant, there is at this stage no barrier whatsoever to four-dimensional topology change.' Sec. III.D: 'The only Lorentzian cobordisms in two dimensions are the torus and the Klein bottle ..., the cylinder ... and the Moebius strip ... The spacetimes of fig. 6b and fig. 6c are explicit examples of Lorentzian topology change' (fig. 6b: S1 u S1 -> empty, 'universe pair-annihilation'; fig. 6c, due to Sorkin: S1 -> empty, 'universe self-annihilation'; reversing V gives the reverse transitions). Sec. IX: 'there are also non-singular topology-changing spacetimes in two dimensions (albeit with closed timelike curves)'. Sec. III.E (restating Geroch [6]): 'in 4 dimensions ... any two externally Euclidean spaces can be connected by an interpolating externally Lorentzian spacetime'.
published_hypotheses: No field equation imposed (the claim is kinematical: 'if a field equation is not imposed').

Classical evolution: an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2, spacelike, joined by a connected interpolating manifold M (Sec. I.A, II.A); S1 or S2 may be empty (creation/annihilation of the universe).
Smooth, non-degenerate ('non-singular') Lorentz metric on all of M, built from a smooth nowhere-vanishing vector field V (Sec. II.B).

Time-oriented metric: 'It is assumed that the metrics being considered are time-oriented' (Sec. II.A); dropping this changes the kinematics (Sec. VII: the RS rule is then no longer required in odd dimensions).
M is NOT required to be foliable by spacelike hypersurfaces; with a foliation, topology cannot change without cuts or holes (Sec. I.A, corollary to Theorem 1).

Existence conditions for the compact case (Reinhart, Sorkin): n even -> chi(M) = 0 (arrangeable by Misner connected sums for n > 2); n odd -> chi(S1) = chi(S2) (RS rule; for n = 3 it forbids every non-identity transition between oriented closed 2-manifolds); n = 2 -> only torus, Klein bottle, cylinder, Moebius strip.

The price is not part of the existence claim but is stated beside it: the 2D examples carry closed timelike curves (Sec. IX), and Theorem 1 forces a CTC in every causally compact topology-changing interpolating spacetime.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED QUALIFIER -- create.py:51-53 ('TOPOLOGY CHANGE IS KINEMATICALLY POSSIBLE. Without a field equation you can build topology-changing spacetimes with non-singular Lorentz metrics ... So it is not forbidden outright') and specthm.py:1156-1157 ('Topology change is kinematically possible') state the claim without the source's 'though there are some constraints' (Sec. III.C). The source's constraints: in odd n the RS rule chi(S1) = chi(S2), which in n = 3 forbids every non-identity oriented closed transition (K7); in n = 2 only the four chi = 0 cobordisms (K6a). Read existentially, the tree's sentence matches the abstract, which is equally unconditional. It is harmless in the tree's dimension: n = 4 has 'no barrier whatsoever' (Sec. III.C, K8). It would matter only if the claim were carried to a specific transition in odd n or in n = 2.

SCOPE OF THE CITED EVIDENCE -- create.py:52 ('Borde exhibits 2-dimensional examples. So it is not forbidden outright') is placed under CREATE, 'bring a throat into existence where there was none' (create.py:41-42), and specthm.py:1146 reads it for throat creation ('(e) Creating a throat is topology change'). Borde's 2D examples are universe pair-annihilation S1 u S1 -> empty (fig. 6b) and self-annihilation S1 -> empty (fig. 6c), with their time reverses. Neither creates a throat in an existing space. K6b enumerates every compact, non-singular, time-oriented 2D Lorentzian cobordism and finds NO change between two non-empty surfaces of different topology, so no 2D example of that kind can exist (the trousers has chi = -1, K5c). The throat-relevant support in the same source is its n = 4 statement (Misner, via Geroch [5]: any two closed 3-manifolds are cobordant, and chi is adjusted by connected sums; K8 builds S^3 -> S^2 x S^1 this way) together with Geroch's externally Lorentzian result for isolated systems (Sec. III.E; Geroch 1967 NAMED-NOT-READ, restated). The conclusion the tree draws is supported. The example it names is not the supporting case.

DROPPED (harmless) -- time-orientation. Borde assumes time-oriented metrics (Sec. II.A), and create.py:51-53 and :188 are silent on it. Dropping it cannot narrow an existence claim: without time-orientation more cobordisms are Lorentzian (Sec. VII, Sorkin [49]: the RS rule is no longer required in odd n). Both 2D examples are time-orientable anyway (K3b; K4a shows that V descends to the Moebius strip).

The tree does state the consequence that matters, CTCs under causal compactness, in the next bullet (create.py:64-66) and in specthm.py:1146-1148, so the price is carried even though the foliation hypothesis is not named.

NOTE ON THE CANONICAL ENTRY -- its name reads 'Borde / Geroch'. The 2D examples are Borde's (fig. 6b) and Sorkin's (fig. 6c, 'due to Sorkin [13]'), not Geroch's. Geroch's contribution to the kinematic side is the 4D externally Lorentzian existence result (Sec. III.E) and, via Misner, the closed 4D case. This is an attribution looseness in the ledger label, not in create.py, which credits Borde for the examples.

K2 (n = 2, 3, 4): Borde's construction g = |V|^2 h - 2 hV hV has det g = -|V|^(2n) and g(V,V) = -|V|^4, so it is non-degenerate and Lorentzian wherever V != 0. K3 builds fig. 6b explicitly on the cylinder [-1,1] x S^1 with V = -2x d_x + d_theta and flat h: det g = -(1+4x^2)^2 < 0 everywhere; V is nowhere zero (time-oriented); both boundary circles are spacelike (g_thth = 3) with V pointing inward at both, so S1 u S1 -> empty; scalar curvature R = -8(2x-1)(2x+1)/(4x^2+1)^3 is finite on the whole strip (smooth, non-singular); the core circle x = 0 is timelike (g_thth = -1), a CLOSED TIMELIKE CURVE, as Borde's Sec. IX says ('albeit with closed timelike curves') and as Theorem 1 requires. K4: V and h are invariant under the Moebius identification (x,theta) ~ (-x, theta+2pi), so the same metric descends to the Moebius strip and gives Sorkin's S1 -> empty (fig. 6c), time-oriented, with the timelike core circle as a CTC (K4c is a documentary step that rests on K3d/K3e). K5: Poincare-Hopf with mixed boundary gives the obstruction chi(M) - chi(S1). That is chi(M) for even n (K5b is documentary, since chi of an odd-dimensional closed manifold is 0) and (chi(S2) - chi(S1))/2 for odd n, which is the RS rule. The trousers has chi = -1 (K5c). K6: enumerating the chi = 0 compact surfaces reproduces Borde's list (torus, Klein, cylinder, Moebius), and the full transition table contains no non-empty -> non-empty change of topology. K7: in n = 3, chi = 2 - 2g is injective, so the RS rule forbids every non-identity oriented transition. K8: n = 4 throat creation S^3 -> S^2 x S^1. (S^2 x D^2) minus a ball has chi = 1; #CP^2 takes it to 2 and #T^4 to 0, so a time-oriented non-degenerate Lorentz metric exists (Misner's procedure, as restated in Sec. III.C). K9: create.py:51-53 and :188 read as quoted, and neither carries time-orientation or 'constraints'. NOT machine-checked: the cobordism facts themselves (that any two closed 3-manifolds are cobordant; Stiefel-Whitney/Pontryagin conditions) and the Reinhart-Sorkin sufficiency direction are infinite-dimensional topology and are taken as restated. Only their Euler-characteristic arithmetic and the explicit 2D metrics are checked.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: did Borde (1994), or Geroch (1967) behind him, lack data that would change 'topology change is kinematically possible'? Evidence says no, in either direction. The claim is a mathematical existence statement with no empirical input: a smooth nowhere-vanishing vector field gives a non-degenerate time-oriented Lorentz metric, and Euler-characteristic and cobordism conditions decide when such a field exists. What was known in 1994 already sufficed: cobordism theory, Reinhart 1963, Sorkin's 2D and RS results, and Misner/Geroch in 4D. The claim is checked here by construction, not by trusting it. K3/K4 build both of Borde's 2D examples explicitly and verify non-degeneracy, smoothness (finite curvature), time-orientation and spacelike boundaries. K8 checks the 4D Euler-characteristic step for throat creation. What came later extends rather than overturns. Degenerate (Morse) metrics widen the kinematically possible class further (Dowker-Surya 1998; Garcia-Heveling 2022), and an explicit non-degenerate 4D wormhole nucleation has been built, with CTCs (Pisana et al. 2025). Later work would bear on this result only if it made kinematic possibility FALSE, and none does. Any later datum or theorem could only restrict what the DYNAMICS permits, which is Theorem 3's domain and a separate ledger key. It could not remove the kinematic existence, which is now shown by explicit example. What M's hypothesis does expose is a scope point, not an error: the tree cites the 2D examples, which are universe creation/annihilation and cannot be throat creation (K6b). The 4D support is in the same paper.
grade_evidence: Statement: create.py:51-53 and :188 reproduce the abstract's existential claim, with its hypotheses 'no field equation' and 'non-singular Lorentz metrics', and name the 2D examples correctly (K1.0-K1.1, K9a-b). Re-derivation agrees: both 2D examples are rebuilt as explicit smooth, non-degenerate, time-oriented metrics on the cylinder and the Moebius strip, with spacelike boundaries and finite curvature (K3a-f, K4a-b), and their CTCs match the source's 'albeit with closed timelike curves' (K3e). The dimension conditions and the 4D throat-creation step check out (K5-K8). No datum enters, so none can move it. Dropped or weakened items, none of which narrows the class the tree uses: (1) the qualifier 'though there are some constraints' (RS rule in odd n; only the four chi = 0 cobordisms in n = 2) is absent at create.py:51-53 and specthm.py:1157, but the tree's setting is n = 4, where the source says 'no barrier whatsoever'; (2) the cited 2D examples are universe creation/annihilation and provably cannot be throat creation in an existing space (K6b), but the same paper's n = 4 statements support the throat case (K8; Geroch III.E restated) and so does the later explicit construction 2505.02210; (3) time-orientation is dropped, and dropping it only enlarges the possible class (Sec. VII); (4) non-foliability is implicit, and the tree carries its consequence, the CTC under causal compactness, in the adjacent bullet (create.py:64-66). Not STANDS-by-default: the source was read (saved alphaXiv full text, md5 asserted), the claim was computed, and every quotation was asserted verbatim. what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any owner uses KINEMATICALLY_POSSIBLE (or 'topology change is kinematically possible') for a specific transition in odd spacetime dimension or in n = 2 between non-empty surfaces, where the RS rule or K6b forbids a non-degenerate time-oriented metric. NARROWED also if an owner reads it as 'possible without CTCs' under causal compactness, since Theorem 1 and the 2D examples' own CTCs forbid that. The tree does neither today (specthm.py:1146-1157 keeps the CTC). NARROWED again if the ledger comes to rest the THROAT-creation (n = 4, open, asymptotically flat) possibility on the 2D examples alone rather than on the n = 4 statements. OPEN on the 4D open-universe case specifically, if Geroch 1967's externally Lorentzian theorem (restated in III.E, NAMED-NOT-READ) were read at source and found to carry a hypothesis Borde's restatement omits. WRONG only if the explicit metrics of K3/K4 failed a check, and they pass.
